ADSL.COMP24FL.CR-8.2.reason: SAP page 9 restricts Completers to the efficacy population, while Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL requires only visit 12 and ENDDT on or after that visit. The efficacy-population condition is absent from the Define-XML rule.

ADSL.BMIBL.CR-5.reason: Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL multiplies HEIGHTBL by 100, and the literal probe states that formula with one-decimal rounding, so the near-zero observed values follow from it; the metres reading rests on the kg/m^2 label. adsl.r L253 divides HEIGHTBL by 100, which shows how the reference was computed and supports that reading, not what Define-XML states.

ADSL.BMIBLGR1.CR-8.3.reason: Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching SAP page 13. BMICAT's '>30' is the stored code for Obese, so comparing that code with the SAP's numeric condition does not establish a conflicting boundary rule; the code-conformance issue is covered by CR-9.

ADSL.BMIBLGR1.CR-8.4.reason: Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching the obese(>=30) condition on SAP page 22. BMICAT's '>30 = Obese' names a category code rather than replacing that derivation condition, so this comparison does not establish contradictory numeric grouping rules.

ADSL.BMIBLGR1.CR-5.reason: The literal Define-XML category rule disagrees with the data. The adjudicator disputes only the proposed SAP/SAS alternative reading; that unsupported explanation does not negate the observed mismatch, including the subject with missing BMI.

ADSL.BMIBLGR1.CR-9.reason: The direct original-XML codelist check represents the 28 invalid obese codes as a separate metadata finding. Retain the literal method comparison separately, including the missing-BMI subject; do not count this legacy codelist observation twice.

ADSL.EDUCLVL.CR-5.reason: Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL names SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU, which the literal probe states and no SC record matches, so every result is missing. The EDLEVEL reading rests on the staged SC test code; adsl.r L257-L260 filters EDLEVEL, showing how the reference was computed rather than a documented rule.

ADSL.DURDIS.CR-8.3.reason: This source-to-source disagreement is context for the audit. A submission program or SAP-only disagreement does not independently establish an outstanding ADaM versus its Define-XML finding.

ADSL.VISNUMEN.CR-8.3.reason: The full Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN comment restricts both branches to DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', whereas its label includes early termination. The completion-only source condition does not implement the label's early-termination scope.
ADSL.VISNUMEN.CR-8.3.title: End-of-treatment visit does not follow the documented completion rule

ADSL.VISNUMEN.CR-8.4.reason: Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN supplies a visit only from a completion record, while SAP page 10 defines end of treatment to include the early termination visit. Correcting the spelling of PROTCOL would not remove that scope difference.
ADSL.VISNUMEN.CR-8.4.title: End-of-treatment visit does not follow the documented completion rule

ADSL.VISNUMEN.CR-5.reason: The literal probe keeps DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED' from Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN, which no record matches, and the on-or-before-Week-24 reading of SAP pages 17 and 40 reproduces the reference. The last-SV reading follows adsl.r L275-L287, which computes VISNUMEN joined at L299, and is correctly presented as the reimplementation's computation, not documentation.
